questions.q: With whom did Yahweh make a covenant?
questions.a: Yahweh made a covenant with Israel in the land of Moab.

questions.q: What previous covenant had Yahweh made with the people of Israel?
questions.a: Yahweh previously made a covenant with Israel at Horeb.

questions.q: Of what did Moses remind all the people of Israel?
questions.a: Moses reminded all them of everything that Yahweh had done in the land of Egypt to Pharaoh, to all his servants, and to all his land.

questions.q: Why did Moses say that the people of Israel needed to be reminded of the great sufferings that their eyes had seen as well as the signs and wonders?
questions.a: Moses said that until that time, Yahweh had not given them understanding about those things.

questions.q: Why did Yahweh lead Israel for 40 years in the wilderness where their clothes and sandals did not wear out and they did not eat any bread or drink any wine or alcoholic drinks?
questions.a: He did those things so that they might know that he is Yahweh their God.

questions.q: What did Israel need to do in order to prosper in everything?
questions.a: They needed to keep the words of this covenant so that they might prosper in everything that they did.

questions.q: Before whom were all of the Israelites standing?
questions.a: All of the Israelites were standing before Yahweh their God.

questions.q: Why were the Israelites standing before Yahweh their God?
questions.a: They were standing before Yahweh in order to enter into the covenant that Yahweh was making with them on that day.

questions.q: What did Yahweh want to do for the people of Israel through this covenant?
questions.a: He wanted to make the people of Israel into a people for himself as he had promised their ancestors.

questions.q: What people were included in the covenant and oath that Yahweh was making with Israel that day in Moab?
questions.a: Everyone standing that day in Moab and also those who were not there with them were included in the covenant that Yahweh was making with Israel.

questions.q: About what were the people of Israel being reminded again?
questions.a: They were being reminded how they had lived in the land of Egypt and how they had traveled through the land that belonged to other people groups after they came out of Egypt.

questions.q: Why were the people being reminded of the disgusting things they had seen when they left Egypt?
questions.a: They were being reminded of the disgusting things they had seen so that there would not be any among them whose heart would turn away from Yahweh, worshiping the gods of those nations.

questions.q: What should the person who hears the words of the curse not say in his heart?
questions.a: The person who hears the words of the curse should not say that he will have peace even though he stubbornly does what he wants.

questions.q: What would happen to the man who says that he will have peace even though he stubbornly does what he wants?
questions.a: Yahweh will not forgive him, Yahweh will be angry with him and all the curses written in the book will happen to him and Yahweh will destroy him and his family forever.

questions.q: What will the future generations and other nations say when they see the plagues on this land and the diseases which Yahweh has sent on them?
questions.a: They will say that Yahweh did this to this land and wonder why he was so angry with the people who lived there.

questions.q: How will people reply when future generations ask why Yahweh did this to the land?
questions.a: The people will say that Yahweh became very angry and brought these curses on their land because they had abandoned the covenant they had made with Yahweh and because they went and worshiped other gods, gods that they had not worshiped before and that he had told them not to worship.

questions.q: What will the people say that Yahweh will do in his anger?
questions.a: The people will say that Yahweh, in his extreme anger, has taken them out of their land and thrown them into another land.

questions.q: To whom do things that are revealed belong?
questions.a: The things that are revealed belong forever to the people of Israel and to their descendants so that they may do all the words of the law.

commentary.text: Moses calls Israel's mercies to remembrance.
The Divine wrath on those who flatter themselves in their wickedness.
The ruin of the Jewish nation.

Verses 1–9 Both former mercies, and fresh mercies, should be thought on by us as motives to obedience. The hearing ear, and seeing eye, and the understanding heart, are the gift of God. All that have them, have them from him. God gives not only food and raiment, but wealth and large possessions, to many to whom he does not give grace. Many enjoy the gifts, who have not hearts to perceive the Giver, nor the true design and use of the gifts. We are bound, in gratitude and interest, as well as in duty and faithfulness, to keep the words of the covenant.

The national covenant made with Israel, not only typified the covenant of grace made with true believers, but also represented the outward dispensation of the gospel. Those who have been enabled to consent to the Lord's new covenant of mercy and grace in Jesus Christ, and to give up themselves to be his people, should embrace every opportunity of renewing their open profession of relation to him, and their obligation to him, as the God of salvation, walking according thereto. The sinner is described as one whose heart turns away from his God; there the mischief begins, in the evil heart of unbelief, which inclines men to depart from the living God to dead idols. Even to this sin men are now tempted, when drawn aside by their own lusts and fancies. Such men are roots that bear gall and wormwood. They are weeds which, if let alone, overspread the whole field. Satan may for a time disguise this bitter morsel, so that thou shalt not have the natural taste of it, but at the last day, if not before, the true taste shall be discerned. Notice the sinner's security in sin. Though he hears the words of the curse, yet even then he thinks himself safe from the wrath of God. There is scarcely a threatening in all the book of God more dreadful than this. Oh that presumptuous sinners would read it, and tremble! for it is a real declaration of the wrath of God, against ungodliness and unrighteousness of man.

Idolatry would be the ruin of their nation. It is no new thing for God to bring desolating judgments on a people near to him in profession. He never does this without good reason. It concerns us to seek for the reason, that we may give glory to God, and take warning to ourselves. Thus the law of Moses leaves sinners under the curse, and rooted out of the Lord's land; but the grace of Christ toward penitent, believing sinners, plants them again in their land; and they shall no more be pulled up, being kept by the power of God.

Moses ends his prophecy of the Jews' rejection, just as St. Paul ends his discourse on the same subject, when it began to be fulfilled, Ro 11:33. We are forbidden curiously to inquire into the secret counsels of God, and to determine concerning them. But we are directed and encouraged, diligently to seek into that which God has made known. He has kept back nothing that is profitable for us, but only that of which it is good for us to be ignorant. The end of all Divine revelation is, not to furnish curious subjects of speculation and discourse, but that we may do all the words of this law, and be blessed in our deed. This, the Bible plainly reveals; further than this, man cannot profitably go. By this light he may live and die comfortably, and be happy for ever.
